definitions.explanation: Strong anger or displeasure aroused by something perceived as unjust, unfair, or wrong.

examples.japanese: {不正|ふせい}に{憤慨|ふんがい}する。
{彼|かれ}の{態度|たいど}に{憤慨|ふんがい}を{覚|おぼ}えた。
examples.english: I felt indignant at his attitude.

examples.japanese: {市民|しみん}は{政府|せいふ}の{対応|たいおう}に{憤慨|ふんがい}している。
examples.english: Citizens are outraged by the government's response.

notes:
COMPOSITION: {憤|ふん} (indignation, resent) + {慨|がい} (lament, deplore). Both characters carry meanings of strong displeasure.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{憤慨|ふんがい}する (to be indignant, to be outraged)
・{憤慨|ふんがい}を{覚|おぼ}える (to feel indignation)
・{憤慨|ふんがい}の{あまり|余り} (out of sheer indignation)
・～に{憤慨|ふんがい}する (to be indignant at ~)

USAGE NOTE: {憤慨|ふんがい} describes righteous anger against perceived injustice or wrongdoing, rather than personal annoyance. It often implies moral outrage.

REGISTER: Formal/literary. Common in news articles and formal written language.

RELATED TERMS:
・{怒|いか}り (anger - more general)
・{激怒|げきど} (fury, rage - more intense)
・{立腹|りっぷく} (anger, offense - formal)
・{義憤|ぎふん} (righteous indignation)
・{慨嘆|がいたん} (lamentation, deploring)

CONTRAST:
・{憤慨|ふんがい}: moral outrage at injustice
・{怒|おこ}る/{怒|いか}る: general anger
・{腹|はら}が{立|た}つ: to get angry (casual)
